name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q01 - Matching principal ores with chemical compositions

questiontext.text:
Match the ores with their correct chemical compositions:

List I (Ore)List II (Composition)
A. Haematitei. \(\mathrm{CuCO_3 \cdot Cu(OH)_2}\)
B. Malachiteii. \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\)
C. Calamineiii. \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\)
D. Copper glanceiv. \(\mathrm{ZnCO_3}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Principal ores of metals are classified according to their chemical nature such as oxides, carbonates, and sulphides.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Haematite is the principal oxide ore of iron with formula \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\). Malachite is a basic carbonate ore of copper with formula \(\mathrm{CuCO_3 \cdot Cu(OH)_2}\). Calamine is a carbonate ore of zinc with formula \(\mathrm{ZnCO_3}\). Copper glance is a sulphide ore of copper with formula \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are Haematite with \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\), Malachite with \(\mathrm{CuCO_3 \cdot Cu(OH)_2}\), Calamine with \(\mathrm{ZnCO_3}\), and Copper glance with \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q02 - Matching metals with their principal ores

questiontext.text:
Match each metal with its corresponding ore:

List I (Metal)List II (Ore)
A. Aluminiumi. Siderite
B. Ironii. Kaolinite
C. Copperiii. Sphalerite
D. Zinciv. Cuprite

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each metal occurs in nature as specific mineral ores from which it can be extracted.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Kaolinite (\([\mathrm{Al_2(OH)_4Si_2O_5}]\)) is a clay mineral ore of aluminium. Siderite (\(\mathrm{FeCO_3}\)) is a carbonate ore of iron. Cuprite (\(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\)) is an oxide ore of copper. Sphalerite, also known as zinc blende (\(\mathrm{ZnS}\)), is a sulphide ore of zinc.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Aluminium pairs with Kaolinite, Iron pairs with Siderite, Copper pairs with Cuprite, and Zinc pairs with Sphalerite.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q03 - Matching refining methods with target metals

questiontext.text:
Match each refining method with the metal commonly purified by it:

List I (Refining Method)List II (Metal)
A. Distillationi. Tin
B. Liquationii. Nickel
C. Zone refiningiii. Zinc
D. Mond processiv. Germanium

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Refining methods are chosen based on differences in physical and chemical properties between the metal and its impurities.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Distillation is suitable for low-boiling metals such as zinc and mercury. Liquation separates low-melting metals like tin from higher-melting impurities on a sloping surface. Zone refining produces ultra-pure semiconductors such as germanium and silicon. The Mond process refines nickel by forming volatile nickel tetracarbonyl.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Distillation matches with Zinc, Liquation matches with Tin, Zone refining matches with Germanium, and Mond process matches with Nickel.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q04 - Matching ore concentration methods with principles

questiontext.text:
Match each concentration method with the physical or chemical property on which it is based:

List I (Method)List II (Underlying Basis)
A. Hydraulic washingi. Solubility of ore in a suitable solvent
B. Magnetic separationii. Difference in wettability of mineral and gangue by oil and water
C. Froth floatationiii. Difference between specific gravities of ore and gangue
D. Leachingiv. Difference in magnetic properties of ore components

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Concentration (benefaction) removes unwanted gangue from powdered ore by exploiting differences in physical or chemical properties.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Hydraulic washing is a gravity separation method based on the difference in specific gravities of ore and gangue particles. Magnetic separation relies on differences in magnetic properties of the ore components. Froth floatation separates sulphide ores using the preferential wetting of mineral particles by oil and gangue by water. Leaching is used when the ore is soluble in a suitable solvent while impurities remain insoluble or separate chemically.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hydraulic washing pairs with specific gravity differences, Magnetic separation pairs with magnetic property differences, Froth floatation pairs with wettability differences, and Leaching pairs with solubility in a suitable solvent.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q05 - Matching metallurgical reagents with their roles

questiontext.text:
Match each reagent used in metallurgical processes with its specific function:

List I (Reagent)List II (Function)
A. Pine oili. Froth stabiliser
B. Cresolii. Collector
C. \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) (with \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) and \(\mathrm{PbS}\))iii. Lowers melting point and increases conductivity of \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)
D. \(\mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}\)iv. Depressant

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specific additives are used in concentration and electrolytic reduction to control surface wetting, froth stability, selectivity, or melt conductivity.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Pine oil acts as a collector in froth floatation by enhancing the non-wettability of mineral particles. Cresol acts as a froth stabiliser to keep the froth intact. Sodium cyanide (\(\mathrm{NaCN}\)) serves as a depressant that selectively prevents \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) from entering the froth while allowing \(\mathrm{PbS}\) to float. Cryolite (\(\mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}\)) is mixed with purified \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) in the Hall-Heroult process to lower the melting point and bring electrical conductivity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Pine oil is a collector, Cresol is a froth stabiliser, \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) is a depressant, and \(\mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}\) lowers the melting point and increases conductivity of \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q06 - Matching metallurgical processes with chemical reactions

questiontext.text:
Match each metallurgical process with its characteristic chemical equation:

List I (Process)List II (Chemical Equation)
A. Calcinationi. \(2\mathrm{ZnS} + 3\mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{ZnO} + 2\mathrm{SO_2}\)
B. Roastingii. \(\mathrm{ZnCO_3}(\mathrm{s}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{ZnO}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{CO_2}(\mathrm{g})\)
C. Mond processiii. \(\mathrm{Zr} + 2\mathrm{I_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZrI_4}\)
D. van Arkel methodiv. \(\mathrm{Ni} + 4\mathrm{CO} \xrightarrow{330\text{--}350\,\mathrm{K}} \mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Conversion of concentrated ores to oxides involves calcination or roasting, whereas vapour phase refining converts impure metals into volatile compounds.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Calcination involves heating carbonate ores to drive off volatile matter, such as \(\mathrm{ZnCO_3}(\mathrm{s}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{ZnO}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{CO_2}(\mathrm{g})\). Roasting heats sulphide ores in a regular supply of air, such as \(2\mathrm{ZnS} + 3\mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{ZnO} + 2\mathrm{SO_2}\). In the Mond process, nickel reacts with carbon monoxide at \(330\text{--}350\,\mathrm{K}\) to form volatile \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}\). In the van Arkel method, crude zirconium is heated with iodine to form volatile \(\mathrm{ZrI_4}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Calcination pairs with \(\mathrm{ZnCO_3}\) decomposition, Roasting pairs with \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) oxidation, Mond process pairs with \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}\) formation, and van Arkel method pairs with \(\mathrm{ZrI_4}\) formation.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q07 - Matching forms of iron with their properties

questiontext.text:
Match each form of commercial iron with its correct description:

List I (Form of Iron)List II (Description)
A. Pig ironi. Made by melting pig iron with scrap iron and coke; contains about \(3\%\) carbon
B. Cast ironii. Purest form of commercial iron, prepared by oxidising impurities in cast iron
C. Wrought ironiii. Obtained directly from the blast furnace; contains about \(4\%\) carbon
D. Sponge ironiv. Porous iron blocks formed by solid-state reduction of iron ore with charcoal

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different forms of iron are distinguished by their method of preparation, carbon content, and physical structure.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Pig iron is obtained directly from the blast furnace and contains about \(4\%\) carbon along with smaller amounts of \(\mathrm{S}\), \(\mathrm{P}\), \(\mathrm{Si}\), and \(\mathrm{Mn}\). Cast iron is made by melting pig iron with scrap iron and coke using a hot air blast, lowering the carbon content to about \(3\%\). Wrought iron is the purest form of commercial iron, prepared from cast iron in a haematite-lined reverberatory furnace. Sponge iron refers to the porous iron blocks formed when iron ore is reduced in the solid state by charcoal.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Pig iron pairs with blast furnace iron containing about \(4\%\) carbon, Cast iron pairs with \(3\%\) carbon iron made with scrap iron and coke, Wrought iron pairs with the purest commercial iron, and Sponge iron pairs with porous blocks from solid-state reduction.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q08 - Matching alloys with their compositions and uses

questiontext.text:
Match each alloy with its constituent metals or characteristic application:

List I (Alloy)List II (Composition / Use)
A. Brassi. Copper and tin
B. Bronzeii. Cutting tools and crushing machines
C. German silveriii. Copper (\(60\%\)) and zinc (\(40\%\))
D. Chrome steeliv. Copper, zinc, and nickel

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Metals such as copper, zinc, and iron are alloyed to improve strength, hardness, and corrosion resistance for specific industrial uses.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Brass is an alloy of copper (\(60\%\)) and zinc (\(40\%\)). Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. German silver consists of copper (\(25\text{--}30\%\)), zinc (\(25\text{--}30\%\)), and nickel (\(40\text{--}50\%\)). Chrome steel is an alloy steel used for cutting tools and crushing machines.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Brass pairs with copper and zinc, Bronze pairs with copper and tin, German silver pairs with copper, zinc, and nickel, and Chrome steel pairs with cutting tools and crushing machines.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q09 - Matching stages in leaching of alumina

questiontext.text:
Match each stage in the leaching of alumina from bauxite with the corresponding chemical or physical operation:

List I (Stage)List II (Operation)
A. Digestioni. Heating \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O}\) at \(1470\,\mathrm{K}\) to obtain pure \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)
B. Neutralisationii. Heating powdered bauxite with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(473\text{--}523\,\mathrm{K}\) and \(35\text{--}36\,\mathrm{bar}\)
C. Seedingiii. Passing \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) gas through sodium aluminate solution
D. Dehydration of hydrated aluminaiv. Adding a small amount of freshly prepared hydrated \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) to induce precipitation

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bauxite contains \(\mathrm{SiO_2}\), iron oxides, and \(\mathrm{TiO_2}\) as impurities, which are removed by chemical leaching to yield pure \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\).

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Digestion involves heating powdered bauxite with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(473\text{--}523\,\mathrm{K}\) and \(35\text{--}36\,\mathrm{bar}\) pressure to extract \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) as sodium aluminate. Neutralisation is carried out by passing \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) gas through the sodium aluminate solution. Seeding refers to adding a small amount of freshly prepared hydrated \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) to induce precipitation of \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O}\). Finally, heating the filtered and dried hydrated alumina at \(1470\,\mathrm{K}\) gives pure \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Digestion pairs with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) treatment, Neutralisation pairs with passing \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), Seeding pairs with adding freshly prepared hydrated \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\), and Dehydration pairs with heating at \(1470\,\mathrm{K}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q10 - Matching refining techniques with underlying principles

questiontext.text:
Match each refining technique with its governing principle:

List I (Technique)List II (Principle)
A. Vapour phase refiningi. Useful for elements in minute quantities whose impurities have similar chemical properties
B. Chromatographic methodii. Low-melting metal flows on a sloping surface away from higher-melting impurities
C. Electrolytic refiningiii. Metal forms an easily decomposable volatile compound with an available reagent
D. Liquationiv. Pure metal deposits at cathode while less basic impurities settle as anode mud

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
High-purity metals are obtained by exploiting differences in volatility, adsorption, electrode potential, or melting point.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Vapour phase refining converts the metal into a volatile compound that is subsequently decomposed to recover the pure metal. Column chromatography is ideal for purifying elements available in minute quantities when impurities have chemical properties close to the element. Electrolytic refining transfers pure metal from the impure anode to the pure cathode, leaving less basic metals as anode mud. Liquation separates low-melting metals like tin by allowing them to flow down a sloping surface.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Vapour phase refining pairs with forming a volatile compound, Chromatographic method pairs with minute quantities and similar properties, Electrolytic refining pairs with cathode deposition and anode mud, and Liquation pairs with flow on a sloping surface.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q11 - Matching blast furnace temperature zones with reactions

questiontext.text:
Match each temperature zone or process in the blast furnace extraction of iron with the corresponding chemical reaction:

List I (Zone / Process)List II (Reaction)
A. \(500\text{--}800\,\mathrm{K}\) (upper part)i. \(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO_3}\)
B. \(900\text{--}1500\,\mathrm{K}\) (\(\mathrm{CO}\) regeneration)ii. \(\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}\)
C. Slag formationiii. \(3\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + \mathrm{CO} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe_3O_4} + \mathrm{CO_2}\)
D. Above \(1073\,\mathrm{K}\) (direct reduction by coke)iv. \(\mathrm{FeO}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s/l}) + \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a blast furnace, iron oxides are reduced stepwise as they descend through zones of increasing temperature, while limestone flux removes silicate impurities.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
At \(500\text{--}800\,\mathrm{K}\) in the upper part of the furnace, \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) is first reduced by \(\mathrm{CO}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}\): \(3\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + \mathrm{CO} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe_3O_4} + \mathrm{CO_2}\). In the \(900\text{--}1500\,\mathrm{K}\) range, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) reacts with hot coke to regenerate \(\mathrm{CO}\): \(\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}\). Limestone decomposes to \(\mathrm{CaO}\), which combines with \(\mathrm{SiO_2}\) gangue to form molten slag: \(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO_3}\). Above \(1073\,\mathrm{K}\), the \(\mathrm{C, CO}\) line lies below the \(\mathrm{Fe, FeO}\) line in the Ellingham diagram, so coke directly reduces \(\mathrm{FeO}\): \(\mathrm{FeO}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s/l}) + \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The \(500\text{--}800\,\mathrm{K}\) zone pairs with \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) reduction to \(\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}\), the \(900\text{--}1500\,\mathrm{K}\) \(\mathrm{CO}\) regeneration pairs with \(\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}\), Slag formation pairs with \(\mathrm{CaSiO_3}\) formation, and Direct reduction above \(1073\,\mathrm{K}\) pairs with \(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe} + \mathrm{CO}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q12 - Matching Ellingham diagram features with thermodynamics

questiontext.text:
Match each feature of an Ellingham diagram (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus}\) versus \(T\) plot) with its thermodynamic interpretation:

List I (Feature)List II (Thermodynamic Interpretation)
A. \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus} > 0\) above the \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus} = 0\) crossing temperaturei. \(\Delta S \approx 0\) as \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gas produces \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gas
B. Downward slope of \(2\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}\)ii. Phase change (\(s \rightarrow l\) or \(l \rightarrow g\)) of the metal
C. Nearly horizontal line for \(\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2}\)iii. \(\Delta S > 0\) because \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) produces \(2\,\mathrm{mol}\) of \(\mathrm{CO}\)
D. Abrupt increase in positive slope on a metal oxide curveiv. The metal oxide decomposes on its own

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The slope of a curve in an Ellingham diagram is \(-\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}S^{\ominus}\), and the sign of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus}\) determines oxide stability.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Above the temperature where a curve crosses \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus} = 0\), the free energy of formation of the oxide becomes positive, so the oxide decomposes on its own. In \(2\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}\), \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gaseous \(\mathrm{O_2}\) yields \(2\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gaseous \(\mathrm{CO}\), giving \(\Delta S > 0\) and a downward slope (\(-\Delta S < 0\)). In \(\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2}\), \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gas produces \(1\,\mathrm{mol}\) of gas, so \(\Delta S \approx 0\) and the line is nearly horizontal. An abrupt increase in positive slope occurs at the temperature where the metal undergoes a phase change (\(s \rightarrow l\) or \(l \rightarrow g\)), increasing reactant entropy and making \(\Delta S\) of oxide formation more negative.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus} > 0\) pairs with spontaneous oxide decomposition, the downward slope of \(2\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}\) pairs with \(\Delta S > 0\), the nearly horizontal \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) line pairs with \(\Delta S \approx 0\), and the abrupt increase in positive slope pairs with a phase change of the metal.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q13 - Matching electrochemical and redox extractions with facts

questiontext.text:
Match each electrochemical or oxidation-reduction extraction process with its corresponding thermodynamic or chemical fact:

List I (Extraction Process)List II (Key Fact)
A. \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) from brinei. \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = +422\,\mathrm{kJ}\), corresponding to \(E^{\ominus} = -2.2\,\mathrm{V}\)
B. \(\mathrm{Au}\) from \([\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-\)ii. \(\mathrm{Zn}\) acts as a reducing agent to displace the noble metal
C. \(\mathrm{Cu}\) from low-grade ore using scrap ironiii. \(\mathrm{Fe}\) goes into solution as \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) while \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) deposits as \(\mathrm{Cu}\)
D. Electrolysis of molten \(\mathrm{NaCl}\)iv. Produces \(\mathrm{Na}\) metal instead of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\)

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electrochemical and hydrometallurgical extractions rely on electrode potentials (\(\Delta G^{\ominus} = -nE^{\ominus}F\)) and displacement redox reactions.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Extraction of \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) from brine (\(2\mathrm{Cl^-} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{OH^-} + \mathrm{H_2} + \mathrm{Cl_2}\)) has \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = +422\,\mathrm{kJ}\) and \(E^{\ominus} = -2.2\,\mathrm{V}\), requiring an external emf greater than \(2.2\,\mathrm{V}\). Gold is recovered from \([\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-\) by displacement using zinc, where \(\mathrm{Zn}\) acts as a reducing agent. In hydrometallurgy of copper with scrap iron, \(\mathrm{Fe}\) is oxidised to \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{Cu}\). Electrolysis of molten \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) yields \(\mathrm{Na}\) metal rather than \(\mathrm{NaOH}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) from brine pairs with \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = +422\,\mathrm{kJ}\) and \(E^{\ominus} = -2.2\,\mathrm{V}\), \(\mathrm{Au}\) recovery pairs with \(\mathrm{Zn}\) as reducing agent, \(\mathrm{Cu}\) with scrap iron pairs with \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) formation and \(\mathrm{Cu}\) deposition, and molten \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) electrolysis pairs with producing \(\mathrm{Na}\) metal.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q14 - Matching ancient Indian metallurgy sites and materials

questiontext.text:
Match each ancient Indian metallurgical site or material with its historical significance:

List I (Site / Material)List II (Significance)
A. Zawar (Rajasthan)i. Deepest ancient gold mines in the world
B. Maski (Karnataka)ii. First mastery of downward distillation of zinc
C. Wootz steeliii. Wrought iron with \(0.25\%\,\mathrm{P}\) showing no corrosion for ~1600 years
D. Iron Pillar (Delhi)iv. High-carbon steel (\(1.0\text{--}1.9\%\,\mathrm{C}\)) derived from the word 'ukku'

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Archaeological excavations and literary records highlight India's ancient expertise in mining, zinc distillation, steel making, and corrosion-resistant wrought iron.

Step 2: Pair-by-Pair Evaluation
Zawar in Rajasthan provides archaeological evidence of zinc production from the 6th or 5th century BCE, where India mastered the downward distillation technique for zinc. Maski in Karnataka has the deepest ancient gold mines in the world. Wootz steel, whose name derives from the word 'ukku', is high-carbon steel containing \(1.0\text{--}1.9\%\) carbon. The Iron Pillar in Delhi is made of wrought iron containing \(0.25\%\,\mathrm{P}\) (along with \(\mathrm{C}\), \(\mathrm{Si}\), \(\mathrm{Mn}\), \(\mathrm{Ni}\), \(\mathrm{Cu}\), \(\mathrm{N}\)) and shows no sign of corrosion after about 1600 years of atmospheric exposure.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Zawar pairs with downward distillation of zinc, Maski pairs with the deepest ancient gold mines, Wootz steel pairs with high-carbon steel from 'ukku', and the Iron Pillar pairs with corrosion-resistant wrought iron containing \(0.25\%\,\mathrm{P}\).
